alertThresholds.scope: this exact disposable topology and package chain

processObserver.method: docker top every 100 ms. Each process is named by the executable its argv runs, not by comm: the Platform Paketi launches every tool through the bundled loader, so comm reports ld-linux-x86-64 for a packaged FFmpeg and ld-musl-x86_64. for a packaged yt-dlp. A loader invocation names its payload after an optional --library-path pair; every other process names its executable in the first token.
processObserver.processesAreNotRequests: One packaged yt-dlp invocation is two processes, the bundled-loader bootloader and the PyInstaller child it forks, both carrying the same argument vector. ytDlpProcessPeak 20 is ten concurrent requests, and is not comparable with records written before issue #68, which counted the child alone.
processObserver.invariantUnchanged: The kernel publishes the argument vector in one step, so a sampled row is either the bracketed comm or a complete command line and never half of one, and a real invocation of either program always carries a full argument vector. The node builds --postprocessor-args ffmpeg:-threads 1 into its only yt-dlp spawn unconditionally, so a genuinely unrestricted process is measurable the first time it is sampled and still fails the lane however briefly it runs. Only a process the observer cannot measure at all is excluded, and an unmeasured process is not evidence of a violation.
processObserver.unwrittenArgvReadsAreNotPasses: Unwritten-argv reads are reported as ytDlpArgvUnwrittenTotal, ffmpegArgvUnwrittenTotal, and unattributedArgvUnwrittenTotal for a loader read that names no tool, and are never folded into ytDlpWithoutFfmpegThreadRestrictionObserved, ffmpegWithoutThreadRestrictionObserved, or ffmpegThreadRestrictionProven.
processObserver.invocationsWithoutMediaWork: The Toolchain Attestation probes the packaged FFmpeg with -version on first use in each main and worker process, and yt-dlp asks the same binary for its bitstream filters. Those processes open no input and do no media work, so ADR 0019 does not reach them: they are reported as ffmpegWithoutMediaInputTotal and excluded from the restriction counts in both directions. An FFmpeg that works on media names its input with -i and is always checked.
processObserver.ffmpegThreadRestrictionDirectlyObserved: This run proves the restriction from FFmpeg itself, not from the yt-dlp command lines. The lane sampled packaged FFmpeg processes working on media in both windows — ffmpegProcessPeak 3 under load and 1 in the probe, across 47 probe observations — every one of them carrying -threads 1, and ffmpegUnrestrictedCommandLines is empty. The lane now refuses to prove the restriction without such an observation, so no later run can pass this flag vacuously.
processObserver.reliabilityAcrossRuns: The observation is reliable rather than lucky: two consecutive runs of the fixed lane on this anchor, 2026-08-14T19:16:34.658Z and 2026-08-14T20:07:15.820Z, each sampled a restricted media FFmpeg in the probe window (ffmpegProcessPeak 1 over 47 observations) and three more under load. The probe re-encodes a twenty-second fixture with --recode-video mkv, which cannot be a stream copy, so FFmpeg lives for seconds rather than the milliseconds a merge of the one-second fixtures takes.
